title: JSON prelude namespace
summary: Typed and schema-less JSON boundaries, path operations, and serialization
lead: JSON is a prelude namespace, not a value type or importable module. Use JSON.Value for any JSON root and JSON.Object, an alias for Map<string, JSON.Value>, for dynamic object keys.
usage: Use `JSON.*` directly without `import`; choose typed parsing whenever the schema is known.

sections.heading: Parse and encode
bullets: `JSON.parse<T>(text)` rejects unknown fields by default; pass `JSON.UnknownFields.Ignore` explicitly when required
`JSON.value(value)` explicitly encodes a composite value; JSON scalars widen implicitly
`JSON.parseWithRest<T>(text)` keeps unknown top-level fields in `rest: JSON.Object`

sections.heading: Dynamic access
bullets: Use `JSON.Object` Map methods and subscripts for one-level dynamic keys
Use `JSON.get<T>()`, `JSON.require<T>()`, `JSON.containsPath()`, `JSON.set()`, and `JSON.remove()` with `JSON.Path` for deep access
Use `JSON.asObject()` / `JSON.asArray()` to unwrap a `JSON.Value` without copying
`JSON.Value` itself has no dot access, subscript, iteration, or `len`
